A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PreferThinker work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and redrawn material.

before.justification: v1 reports original PreferImg and PickaPic evaluations, ablations, qualitative assessments and a 100-participant study of visual preference elements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3, the robustness evaluation and the user study relocated to Figure S1.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the five-attribute profiles, predict-then-assess procedure, Qwen2.5-VL-7B model, SFT followed by GRPO, and similarity, format and accuracy rewards. Expanded attribution and redrawn diagrams do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use PreferImg/PreferImg-CoT with single- and multiple-preference users and user-grouped PickaPic. The single-image assessment and personalized generation demonstrations are also retained.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1 and 3 and the reference-count robustness plots are unchanged. Newly cited PAL and PrefGen are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the 1,500-user PreferImg benchmark, its splits, 894 PickaPic samples, evaluation measures and training settings. Tables S1–S3 are relocated without changing their reported settings.

E4.justification: The SFT/RL and prediction-reward ablations, reference-count robustness tests, single-image scoring, generation demonstrations and failure case are retained. The redesigned displays do not introduce new analytical questions or cases.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the benchmark results. Statistical uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: In Figure 2, v3 changes Image A's color score from 2 to 1 and saturation score from 3 to 1, matching the unchanged appendix example (v1 Figure S8; v3 Figure S9). Its displayed total nevertheless remains 12 rather than 9. Tables 1–3, robustness curves and other matched results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same SFT objective, GRPO formulation and reward definitions. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems or proofs in the appendices.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about interpretable personalized assessment, PreferImg-CoT, the prediction reward, superior performance and usefulness for personalized generation.

C2.justification: Appendix E.4 replaces the broad synthetic-to-real preference gap discussion with more specific limitations of the five visual attributes, identifying omitted image semantics and user backgrounds such as age, gender and culture. Future work consequently emphasizes incorporating additional preference factors; the failure example is unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a Project Page link and removes v1's statement that code and data will be released. It also explicitly states the 288-word preference vocabulary size. Training details and prompt templates are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the linked resources are available.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to PAL and PrefGen. Section 3.2 now credits PrefGen as inspiration for synthetic-data construction and the selection of 190K initial prompts. The broader positioning against existing assessment methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise limited abstract editing, expanded profile-selection explanation in Section 3.1 and Appendix B.1, the rewritten limitations paragraph, and added acknowledgments and conference headers. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The central assessment and reward examples are substantially enlarged and reorganized, placing horizontal reference-image panels above the reasoning. Figure 1 is redrawn, robustness plots receive shared external legends, and tables are restyled. The user-study graphic moves from v1 Figure 3 to v3 Figure S1. These changes substantially revise the main visual presentation while retaining most evidence.

improvement.justification: Clearer central figures, explicit PrefGen attribution and more specific real-user limitations modestly improve readability and transparency. Figure 2's incomplete score correction leaves a local inconsistency—its revised components sum to 9 while the total remains 12—but does not change the selected image or benchmark findings. The underlying empirical support is otherwise unchanged.
